Here is the rest of your master plan, picking up right where we left off.

---

## ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING & DECLUTTER CHECKLIST

**Golden Rule for Cross-Country Decluttering:** Movers and containers charge by weight or cubic feet. Ask yourself: *"Would I pay $20 to ship this item 2,400 miles?"* If the answer is no, sell, donate, or toss it.

### 1. Garage, Basement, & Storage (Weeks 6–5)
*Time Estimate: 4–8 hours | Priority: HIGH (Do this first)*
- [ ] **J** **Declutter:** Toss old paint, aerosols, propane tanks, motor oil, and harsh chemicals (movers are legally barred from taking hazardous materials). Drop them at an Ohio hazardous waste facility.
- [ ] **M** **Declutter:** Sell or donate heavy seasonal gear you won't need in Oregon (e.g., heavy-duty snowblowers if moving to the milder Willamette Valley, rusty yard tools, spare lumber).
- [ ] **M** **Pack:** Bundle long-handled tools together with zip ties. Drain fuel and oil from any gas-powered lawn tools completely before packing.
- [ ] **P** **Pack:** Pack holiday decorations, camping gear, and Keepsake boxes. Use plastic bins if you already have them, and tape the lids shut.

### 2. Guest Room, Office, & Books (Weeks 5–4)
*Time Estimate: 3–5 hours | Priority: MED*
- [ ] **J** **Declutter:** Shred old bills and tax returns older than 7 years. Donate books you won't read again (books are the heaviest items you own).
- [ ] **P** **Pack:** Pack books ONLY in small boxes (under 40 lbs) so the bottoms don't blow out. Pack spines facing down or flat.
- [ ] **M** **Pack:** Take photos of the back of your computer/TV setups so you remember where cables go. Coil cords and put them in labeled Ziploc bags taped to the item they belong to. Keep critical work laptops with you in the car.

### 3. Living Room & Dining Room (Weeks 4–3)
*Time Estimate: 4–6 hours | Priority: MED*
- [ ] **J** **Declutter:** Sell cheap particle-board furniture (IKEA bookshelves, cheap coffee tables). They often don't survive the vibrations of a 2,400-mile truck ride and cost more to ship than replace.
- [ ] **P** **Pack:** Wrap framed art and mirrors in bubble wrap and use picture boxes. Put a masking-tape "X" across large glass frames to prevent shattering if impacted.
- [ ] **M** **Pack:** Disassemble dining table legs and shelving. Put all screws, bolts, and Allen wrenches into a Ziploc bag, label it clearly, and tape it securely to the underside of the furniture piece.

### 4. Bedrooms & Closets (Weeks 3–2)
*Time Estimate: 3–5 hours | Priority: MED*
- [ ] **J** **Declutter:** If it doesn't fit, is stained, or hasn't been worn in 12 months, donate it. (Note: Keep rain jackets and layers for Oregon!).
- [ ] **P** **Pack:** Leave clothes in dresser drawers if doing DIY (take drawers out to carry the frame, then slide them back in the truck). If using movers, ask if they allow clothes in drawers— otherwise, use wardrobe boxes or heavy-duty trash bags poked through the hangers.
- [ ] **M** **Pack:** Pack extra linens, pillows, and out-of-season shoes in large boxes (they are light, so large boxes won't get too heavy). Set aside 1 set of sheets and 2 towels per person for the final week.

### 5. Kitchen & Pantry (Weeks 2–1)
*Time Estimate: 6–10 hours (Always takes the longest!) | Priority: HIGH*
- [ ] **J** **Declutter:** Toss expired spices, half-empty sauces, and duplicate utensils. Plan meals for the last 2 weeks to "eat down" the freezer and pantry. Do not ship heavy canned goods or glass jars across the country—donate unopened food to an Ohio food bank.
- [ ] **P** **Pack:** Pack plates **vertically** on their edges (like records), cushioned with packing paper or dish towels—flat-stacked plates break much easier.
- [ ] **M** **Pack:** Box up small appliances (Instant Pot, blender, toaster) first, leaving only the coffee maker and 1 skillet/pot for the final week. Switch to paper plates for the last 4 days.

### 6. Bathrooms & Laundry (Week 1)
*Time Estimate: 2 hours | Priority: LOW*
- [ ] **J** **Declutter:** Toss expired medications, old makeup, and almost-empty shampoo bottles.
- [ ] **P** **Pack:** Take the tops off any liquid bottles you are keeping, place a piece of plastic wrap over the opening, and screw the cap back on to prevent pressure leaks across mountain passes. Put all liquids inside sealed Ziploc bags.

---

## SERVICES & SUBSCRIPTIONS TIMELINE

- **4 Weeks Out (M):** Cancel local Ohio memberships (gym, local car wash club, CSA boxes, country clubs/recreation centers) which often require a 30-day billing notice.
- **3 Weeks Out (P):** Notify home security company (ADT, SimpliSafe, Ring) to schedule equipment deactivation or transfer.
- **2 Weeks Out (J):** Schedule Ohio utility shut-offs (Electric, Gas, Water, Sewer, Trash, Internet) for **the day after** moving day (you do not want to be cleaning in the dark with no running water on your last day).
- **2 Weeks Out (J):** Schedule Oregon utility turn-ons for **the day before** your arrival.
- **1 Week Out (P):** Pause or update delivery addresses for Amazon, Chewy (critical for dog food!), meal kits, and streaming services (Hulu Live/YouTube TV need your new zip code for local channels). Return any borrowed library books or rented cable modems/routers!

---

## 8-WEEK PHONE-SYNCABLE REMINDER CALENDAR

*Tip: Copy and paste these into your shared Google/Apple Calendar as "All-Day" events on Mondays or Saturdays so they pop up on both of your phones.*

* **8 Weeks Out — [MOVE] Lock in Logistics:** Book moving company or truck/POD. Book car shipping (if using). Schedule dog's pre-move vet checkup.
* **7 Weeks Out — [MOVE] Housing & Route:** Finalize Oregon housing/lease. Map driving route to Oregon and book dog-friendly hotels for every night on the road. Schedule Oregon internet installation.
* **6 Weeks Out — [MOVE] Declutter & Supplies:** Give formal 60/30-day notice to Ohio landlord. Buy boxes/tape. Declutter and pack Garage/Storage. Drop off hazardous waste.
* **5 Weeks Out — [MOVE] Car & Guest Rooms:** Take car in for cross-country maintenance check. Pack Guest Room, Office, and Books.
* **4 Weeks Out — [MOVE] Cancel Local Services:** Cancel Ohio gym/local subscriptions. Pack Living Room and Dining Room decor. Request vet records & refill dog meds for 60 days.
* **3 Weeks Out — [MOVE] Utilities & Address:** Submit USPS Change of Address. Schedule Ohio utility shut-offs and Oregon utility start dates. Pack Bedrooms/Closets (except 2 weeks of clothes).
* **2 Weeks Out — [MOVE] Confirmations & Kitchen Start:** Call movers/car shippers to confirm arrival windows. Update auto/renters insurance to Oregon effective on move date. Pack 75% of Kitchen.
* **1 Week Out — [MOVE] Final Countdown:** Return cable boxes/library books. Change Chewy/Amazon addresses. Pack remaining items. Defrost fridge (24 hrs prior). Pack Car & Dog Essentials kits.

---

turns.text:
### 1. Simple Box-Labeling System (Color + Short Tag)

Movers won’t read paragraphs written on cardboard, and they stack boxes on top of each other (hiding the top flaps). This system uses **colored tape** and a **3-part alphanumeric code** so anyone carrying a box knows exactly where it goes from 10 feet away.

#### Step A: The Color-Code (Buy a $12 multi-pack of colored duct/painter's tape)
Tape a 4-inch strip of colored tape on **two adjacent sides** (not the top!) of each box, and stick a matching piece of tape on the doorframe of the corresponding room in your Oregon home when you arrive.

* 🟨 **YELLOW = Kitchen / Dining (`KIT`)**
* 🟦 **BLUE = Primary Bedroom (`BED`)**
* 🟩 **GREEN = Living Room (`LIV`)**
* 🟧 **ORANGE = Office / Guest Room (`OFF`)**
* 🟪 **PURPLE = Bathrooms / Laundry (`BTH`)**
* ⬜ **WHITE / BLACK = Garage / Storage (`GAR`)**
* 🟥 **RED = OPEN FIRST / CAR ONLY (`ESS`)** *(Put a big X of red tape on boxes that MUST NOT go on the moving truck)*

#### Step B: The Short Tag Format
Write this in thick black Sharpie directly on the colored tape (or right below it) on **two sides** of the box:

> **`[ROOM]-[BOX #] | [PRIORITY 1-3]`**  
> *(Underneath, write 2–3 words max of general contents—never write high-value specifics like "Jewelry" or "PS5", just write "Misc" or "Office" for security).*

**Priority Key:**
* **`P1`** = Unpack Day 1 (Bedding, coffee maker, dog supplies, basic pans)
* **`P2`** = Unpack Week 1 (Everyday clothes, standard kitchenware, toiletries)
* **`P3`** = Unpack Whenever (Books, decor, out-of-season gear, storage)

**Examples of what to write on the box:**
* **`KIT-01 | P1`** *(Coffee maker, mugs, skillet)*
* **`KIT-14 | P3`** *(Baking pans, holiday platters)*
* **`LIV-04 | P2`** *([FRAGILE] Lamps, router/cables)*

*Pro-Tip for numbering:* Don't worry about keeping room numbers sequential as you pack. Either number boxes sequentially across the whole house (`01` to `85`) OR let each room have its own count (`KIT-01`, `KIT-02` / `BED-01`, `BED-02`). Just log each one in your sheet as you tape it shut!

---

### 2. What to Encode in Each QR Code & How to Generate Them

Instead of linking to a website (which fails if you don't have cell service/Wi-Fi during unloading), encode **plain text** right into the QR code so that scanning a sealed box with your phone camera immediately pops up its exact contents on your screen.

#### Exact One-Line Text Format to Encode:
```text
KIT-01 | P1 | TRUCK | Fragile:Y | Coffee maker, grinder, 4 mugs, silverware
```

#### Quick Copy-Paste Instructions for Generating QR Codes Free:
1. **Automatically inside Google Sheets (Fastest for bulk):**
   * Put your one-line text string above into **Cell K2** of your inventory sheet.
   * In **Cell L2**, paste this exact formula:
     `=IMAGE("https://quickchart.io/qr?text=" & ENCODEURL(K2) & "&size=150")`
   * Hit Enter—a scannable QR code will instantly appear inside the cell! Drag the formula down for all your boxes, print that column, cut them out, and glue/tape them over the `[QR]` spot on your labels.
2. **One-by-One via Free Web Tool (No account needed):**
   * Go to **qr-code-generator.com** or **goqr.me** in your browser.
   * Select **"Plain Text"** (not URL), paste your one-line text (`KIT-01 | P1 | TRUCK | Fragile:Y | Coffee maker...`), and click **Download PNG** to print.

### 1. PDF Layout Spec (Exact Dimensions)

To fit a **3-column x 5-row** grid of **2" x 4" labels** on a single page without clipping, orient the labels **horizontally** (3.5"–3.6" wide x 1.6"–2" tall) in **Landscape** mode, or use these exact table/page specs in your PDF maker:

* **Page Size:** US Letter (11.0" wide x 8.5" high — **Landscape**)
* **Page Margins:** Top/Bottom: `0.25"` | Left/Right: `0.25"` *(Note: Since 3 x 4" = 12" and US Letter is 11" wide, standard 3x5 sheets on 8.5x11" use **3.5" wide x 1.6" high** cells so all 15 fit cleanly with 0.25" margins. If you are printing on 12"x18" or scaling to fit, set exact cell size to **3.5" W x 1.6" H** for true 100% scale on Letter, or **4.0" W x 2.0" H** and select "Fit to Printable Area" in the print dialog).*
* **Grid Layout:** 3 Columns x 5 Rows (Zero cell spacing / collapsed borders)
* **Font:** `Courier New` (Monospace), Size `8.5 pt` or `9 pt`, Line Spacing `1.0` (Single)
* **1" QR Box Zone:** The right-hand `[   1" QR   ]` block spans 5 lines vertically x 11 characters wide, creating an exact `1.0" x 1.0"` square on paper to glue/paste your QR image over.
